This workbook is the Phase 1 database the phone app will read. Example rows are flagged EXAMPLE — delete or convert them before going live, and do not reuse their IDs.
RULES  —  read these before adding real data
Once an ID is used (asset, work order, part, PM, technician, or location), it is retired forever — even if you delete or cancel the record. Skipping numbers is fine. Reusing numbers is not.
Do not rename headers or sheets
The app reads exact sheet names and exact column header names (asset_id, wo_id, and so on). You can add columns later if needed, but do not rename, reorder-by-cutting, or delete the existing headers.
Each data sheet is an Excel table. Click the last cell in the table and press Tab to get a new row. That keeps filters, dropdowns, and the app's table range intact.
Status, type, category, priority, craft, and similar fields have dropdowns fed by the Lists sheet. If you need a new choice, add it on Lists — don't type a one-off spelling.
Temperatures in °F, pressure in psi, volume in gallons, length in feet, weight in pounds, power in hp. Do not use °C, bar, liters, meters, kilograms, or kW.
EXAMPLE rows are not live data

Every starter row has data_flag = EXAMPLE. Before the app goes live, delete those rows or change data_flag to REAL after you have reviewed them. Keep the high-water marks below — do not restart IDs at 0001 if 0001-0005 were already used.
Dates are local Pacific Time in MM/DD/YYYY. Date-and-time fields use MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM (24-hour). Money is US dollars.

qr_url follows a stable pattern the app will keep forever: https://cmms.local/a/AST-0001 for assets and https://cmms.local/w/WO-000001 for work orders. Replace only the host (cmms.local) when the app is published. Do not change the /a/ and /w/ paths.
ID CONVENTIONS  —  uppercase, hyphen, zero-padded, never recycled

High-water marks above already count the five example rows on each main sheet. After you delete EXAMPLE rows, do not go back to AST-0001 — start real assets at AST-0006 (and the same idea for the other IDs). When you issue a new ID, bump the Next ID in this table so the next person (or the app) does not collide.

This sheet — conventions, rules, and the map of the workbook.

A Location (LOC-0001 Bottling Hall) holds many Assets. An Asset may have a parent Asset (AST-0002 Rotary Filler belongs to AST-0001 Bottling Line 1). Work orders point at one Asset and may be assigned to a Technician by name. A work order can be born from a PM schedule (pm_id). Parts used on a job are listed in WO_Parts (wo_id + part_id + qty + cost). A Part can also list the assets it fits in used_on_asset_ids (comma-separated, e.g. AST-0002, AST-0003). Meter readings belong to one Asset and are stamped with a local Pacific timestamp. Source is Manual today; Ignition later.

Go to Assets, Tab off the last row, assign the next AST- ID, fill name/category/location, set criticality (A = line-stopper, B = important, C = convenience), enter nameplate data in hp / volts / psi / gallons, and paste the qr_url once the label is printed.

Go to WorkOrders, assign the next WO- ID, pick the asset, type, priority, and status. Write the problem in plain language. Assign a technician. The app will use the same columns, so what you type here is what shows on the phone.

Go to PM_Schedules. Calendar PMs use unit days/weeks/months. Meter PMs use hours or cycles and need Meter_Readings to stay current. Put the SOP name in sop_ref and any kit in parts_kit (part IDs, comma-separated).
Update qty_on_hand on Parts. When a part is used on a job, add a WO_Parts row and leave cost = qty x unit_cost_usd (you can type the amount).
Add a Meter_Readings row: asset, number, unit (hours, cycles, psi, °F, gallons), and the Pacific timestamp. This is also where Ignition will write later.
Failure stops the bottling line or creates a safety / product-loss risk. Target same-day response.
Important utility or downstream equipment. Plan repair; temporary workaround may be acceptable.
Convenience or spare. Schedule when convenient.
Safety, spill, or the line is down now.
Will stop the line or create a quality problem if not handled this shift / next shift.
Planned or can wait for the next available window.
